first.rationale: Aggressive competitor pricing creates an immediate acquisition threat among price-sensitive SMBs, and memory_73 indicates targeted pricing can lift acquisition and revenue. Before committing, verify whether that lift sustained qualified revenue after discounting, including retention and unit economics. Verify memory_86 as the strongest alternative tied to the current onboarding decline. Current intent is a narrowly targeted, guarded pricing experiment rather than a broad discount rollout.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source directly addresses the current 4% completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, aligning with sustainable qualified revenue. Do not pursue promotional pricing: despite short-term signup and qualified-revenue lift, its verified cohort suffered 30-day retention of -12% and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Activation messaging remains plausible, but its downstream value was not verified and the onboarding evidence is stronger.

final2.rationale: Proceed with shortened onboarding despite the competitor’s deeper price cut. Verified evidence shows improved completion, faster time-to-value, and higher 30-day retention, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is not justified: the verified targeted-discount cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed at first renewal, directly conflicting with the long-term objective. The new competitive pressure raises uncertainty and warrants separate retention handling, but it does not overturn the available experiment evidence.
